title: Index Removal
statement: An array is called good when it is non-decreasing and every adjacent difference is at most k. Given a good array of length n, the task is to answer independently for every index: after that element is deleted, what is the minimum total number of unit decrements applied to the remaining elements needed to make the array good again. Constraints reach n up to 2*10^5 with values up to 10^9.
